cues.text: In this town, everyone got a superpower at eighteen.
Mine was one daisy. I hated it.
My twin brother's was taking other people's powers.
He came back with a hundred of them, and he burned my town.
Then I found out what the daisy was. My power was life.
So I told him, "I know how to beat you."
That was a lie. I had no idea.
I was still getting up out of the mud
when Tip ran at him. Tip, whose whole power was knowing which way was north.
My brother looked him in the face.
And flicked him, too.
Tip went up over the rooftops, shouting, "North! I am going north!"
I did not think. I put both arms into the mud.
They glowed green.
Roots came out of the ground and raced after him,
over the pig pen, over the well, faster than he fell.
And just before he hit the road, the roots grew one giant leaf.
Tip landed in it like a baby in a blanket.
Then my knees gave out.
A leaf that big takes a lot out of you.
And I could do that the whole time? Nobody told me.
My brother pointed at me.
The tip of his finger glowed red.
Lava came out of it.
I grew a tree under my own feet, and it threw me out of the way.
I got one breath.
Then he was flying. Of course he could fly.
So I grew a leaf across my back, as wide as a door,
and I jumped, and the wind took me.
I was gliding. Me. The daisy boy.
He stopped chasing me.
He held out one arm, shut one eye, and made a spear of fire. White hot.
It went through my wing like paper.
I fell. Luckily, not far.
I landed in the square, and I looked up.
My mother. Bo. Mira. Tip. Half the town, hiding behind the well.
I had led him straight to everyone I loved.
Bo said, "Was that the plan?" It was not a plan.
Far down the street, my brother raised both hands,
and a wall of lava came up out of the road.
As high as the bell.
He pushed it towards us.
I had no leaf for that. No tree. No idea.
So I raised one finger.
And I closed my eyes.
I felt the heat on my face.
Then I did not.
I opened them.
The wall of lava was a wall of grass.
Do not ask me how. I still do not know.
But it was mine now.
So I pushed it back.
And as it went, it grew roses. Then it grew the thorns.
My brother had a hundred powers, and not one second to pick one.
It hit him like a garden falling off a roof.
He stood there, swaying, with a rose in his hair.
This was my chance. I ran at him.
And everything went slow.
I thought: Brother. Why did you choose this path?
I do not see an enemy.
I see my brother.
He was so dizzy that he went down on his knees.
He looked up at me.
Then he looked down, and he said,
"You win. Do it."
I raised my hand.
A power that gives life could take one. He knew it. So did I.
I opened it, and I held it out.
And I smiled, and I said, "Let's go back to the way it was. Okay?"
He looked at me like he was waiting for something worse.
He believed he could not be forgiven.
He was wrong, and I stood there until he knew it.
He looked at my hand.
And he shook it.
One week later.
My brother walked from village to village, and gave every power back.
Bo got his jump. He has not stopped since.
And the two of us fixed every house we broke. He carries. I grow the wood.
He says sorry to the pigs every morning. The pigs are thinking about it.
That night, my mother set four plates.
And for the first time in ten years, three of us sat down.
Outside his door, there is one small daisy. I did not put it there.
Like and subscribe for more.
